plotSections.title: Walker's gold hand and departure
bullets: Walker tells Quaylin he turned his hand gold by putting it into cold molten-looking water while swimming underwater, with no loon folk nearby.
He tested only his hand because he panicked and thought he had lost it.
Quaylin compares the result to a Midas-like alchemical process.
Plymouth confirms he secured several pounds of dragon gizzard.
Walker leaves Qualin's Quax to seek funds from the Haven Hold dragon; Quaylin says potions may go on sale later.

plotSections.title: Invisible party on the boat
bullets: After Walker’s scene pauses, the main party remains invisible on the boat and still cannot hear one another.
Closing the door left the ship floating in place; the boat can list side to side but is otherwise back to normal except for the invisibility and silence.
Ord’s oily dragon-vessel outline is still faintly visible but has mostly dissipated.
A floating spectral door remains closed where the doorway was.
Gerk is still confused and largely unable to act normally.

plotSections.title: Cross-realm economics
bullets: Gerk asks whether gold has the same value across Atlas’s realms.
The DM confirms exchange differences exist and notes the party has access to six of eight Arch realms.
The party could theoretically create a cross-realm market and exploit foreknowledge of keystone door openings to cause economic hardship against the lich.
Gerk jokingly names the market The Gerkin.

plotSections.title: Sylan tries to snap Gerk out of confusion
bullets: Sylan decides against reopening the spectral door now that the ship seems stabilized.
With no ship paper available, Sylan writes detect magic on the floor using coins.
Sylan physically wrangles the invisible Gerk by slapping, grabbing, and shaking him under his chitin armor.
Gerk feels accosted, grabs back, and becomes slightly more lucid enough to recognize his boat and a smaller person’s wrist in his grip.
Gerk fails a wisdom save and then tries to swing Sylan around.
In a strength contest Gerk wins with an effective 21, and Sylan cannot budge him.
Ciri watches the invisible struggle without being able to see what is happening.

chronologicalEvents: Walker finishes explaining his gold hand to Quaylin.
Plymouth confirms he bought several pounds of dragon gizzard.
Walker leaves Qualin's Quax to negotiate with the Haven Hold dragon.
The scene shifts to the main party, still invisible and unable to hear each other on the boat.
The party confirms Ord’s oily outline is fading and Gerk remains confused.
The group discusses cross-realm gold values and the idea of a keystone-based stock market against the lich.
Sylan notes the floating spectral door is now closed.
The DM confirms the ship is floating in place and otherwise back to normal aside from invisibility and silence.
Sylan writes detect magic on the floor with coins.
Sylan begins physically wrangling invisible Gerk to break the confusion effect.
Gerk grabs back and becomes slightly more lucid.
Gerk tries to swing Sylan around; Sylan wins the strength contest on Gerk’s side with a 21 and cannot be moved.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen, Gatekeeper of The Reach.
notes: Explains his gold hand came from putting his hand into cold molten-looking water while swimming underwater.
Only his hand was affected because he panicked.
Leaves Qualin's Quax to seek a loan from the Haven Hold dragon.
personality: Sometimes acts first and thinks later when curious.
quotesThemes: Of course I put my hand in it because it was cold molten stuff.

notes: Hears Walker’s full gold-hand story.
Confirms Plymouth bought several pounds of dragon gizzard.
Tells Walker he may come back later when potions might be on sale.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer and party ally who guides the new keepers.
notes: Secured several pounds of dragon gizzard at Qualin's Quax.
Previously signaled Walker not to discuss the gold hand further in the shop.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian Doorman and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: Remains on the invisible, silent party boat under the confusion effect.
Feels accosted by unseen hands as Sylan tries to shake him back to lucidity.
Grabs back, becomes slightly more lucid, and recognizes his boat plus a smaller person’s wrist in his hand.
Fails a wisdom save.
Wins a strength contest with an effective 21 and cannot be moved or swung successfully by Sylan.
Sees the closed floating spectral door and decides not to reopen it.
Writes detect magic on the boat floor using coins because there is no ship paper or log onboard.
Physically wrangles invisible Gerk to break the confusion effect.
Loses a strength contest against Gerk despite grabbing him under his armor.
Remains on the invisible party boat.
His oily dragon-vessel outline is still faintly visible but has mostly dissipated.
Remains on the invisible party boat watching the chaos.
Cannot see the invisible struggle between Sylan and Gerk.

Spectral Door.existing: A mysterious spectral door resembling Gerk's shield form.
notes: Now appears as a closed floating spectral door where the doorway was.
Sylan had planned to open it again but decides against it after the ship stabilizes.

Confusion Effect.existing: A spell effect that leaves its victim confused and unable to act meaningfully.
notes: Still afflicts Gerk on the boat.
Sylan’s physical wrangling only partially improves Gerk’s lucidity.
Gerk fails a wisdom save during the attempt to shake him out of it.

Lich.existing: An unidentified lich whose phylactery may be hidden among his chess pieces.
notes: The DM says the party could use cross-realm trade and keystone door timing as insider knowledge to cause economic hardship against the lich.

Keystones.existing: Magical stones used to open and connect Atlas’s Arch realms.
notes: The party currently has access to six of Atlas’s eight Arch realms, enough to manipulate inter-realm trade if they choose.

newTerms.name: Loon folk
notes: Aquatic people Quaylin despises.
Said to be biologically inferior, unable to walk on land, and prone to trapping themselves in shallow puddles.

newTerms.name: The Gerkin
notes: Joking name Gerk proposes for a cross-realm stock market using the party’s keystone access.

newTerms.name: Cross-realm trade manipulation
notes: With access to six of eight Arch realms, the party could exploit door-opening timing for economic leverage against the lich.
